facts.raw_span: asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
broken hairs were not seen
result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
Antinuclear antibody: Negative
Antidouble-stranded DNA antibody: Negative

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves, localized linear hair loss, and histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and hyaline fat necrosis are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune condition that can cause skin and hair lesions.

The patient's symptoms of linear hair loss, hair thinning, and dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation are consistent with lichen planopilaris, a condition that can cause hair loss and skin lesions.

The patient's presentation of linear hair loss, hair thinning, and bandlike grooved alopecic lesions on the frontal scalp are consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia, a condition that can cause hair loss and scarring.
The patient's symptoms of hair loss, hair thinning, and absence of broken hairs are consistent with pseudopelade of Brocq, a condition that can cause scarring hair loss.
The patient's presentation of hair loss, hair thinning, and negative hair pull test are consistent with alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that can cause hair loss.

The patient's histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates, hyaline fat necrosis, and positive direct immunofluorescence are consistent with morphea, a condition that can cause skin lesions and scarring.

rationales.F03: The presence of two long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches is more typical of frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F08: The presence of predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F09: The presence of inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F10: The presence of granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F11: The absence of antinuclear antibody makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.
rationales.F12: The absence of antidouble-stranded DNA antibody makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: Discoid lupus erythematosus best explains the histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates, hyaline fat necrosis, and positive direct immunofluorescence, despite negative antinuclear and antidouble-stranded DNA antibodies.
